findings.claim: key_bump_due is recomputed from whatever call failed, not from the transfers.create outcome, so a pending key bump is lost when a later attempt fails before create, and a bump is set when create was never called.
findings.evidence: writeFailure always writes key_bump_due = received (lines 359-368). Example: attempt n gets a stored 4xx/5xx from transfers.create, so key_bump_due becomes true. Attempt n+1 then fails earlier with no response (refunds.list or paymentIntents.retrieve timeout at lines 193/206), and writeFailure sets key_bump_due=false. Attempt n+2 then reuses the old key, Stripe replays the cached error, and one of the 5 attempts is wasted toward manual handling. The reverse also happens: a received 4xx from refunds.list or paymentIntents.retrieve (e.g. a 404) sets key_bump_due=true although transfers.create was never sent with that key. The tests only cover 5xx and timeouts thrown by transfers.create itself (payouts-transfer.test.mjs lines 173-234).
findings.fix: Track which call failed (for example, wrap createTransfer and tag its error). Set key_bump_due=true only when transfers.create got a received non-409/429 response. Otherwise keep the stored value (key_bump_due = key_bump_due OR $5). Add a DB test: a 400 from create, then a refunds.list timeout, then success with key_version 2 and one transfer.

findings.claim: transferOne cancels a re-claimed payout on refund without the take-over check, even when an earlier attempt may have created a Stripe transfer, so a paid-out refunded request can end up cancelled and is never surfaced.
findings.evidence: cancelRefunded runs a take-over only for status='failed' AND attempts>0 (lines 76-109), and it silently `continue`s when transfers.list throws (line 95). An expired 'transferring' lease (worker killed after transfers.create, before writeSuccess) is re-claimed in transferOne. The DB check at lines 178-184 (or the refunds.list check at 194-203) then sets status='cancelled' with no findExistingTransfer. Recovery then depends only on a transfer.created webhook (webhook.mjs line 255 accepts cancelled rows with attempts>0). The job never reconciles it, and payoutsNeedingAttention never counts it. No test covers an expired lease combined with a refund.
findings.fix: In transferOne, when attempt > 1 (or key_bump_due / last_error is set) and the payment has a refund, run findExistingTransfer first. If a transfer is found, write paid + refunded_after_payout. Only otherwise cancel. Log errors in the cancelRefunded catch. Add a DB test for an expired lease, a transfer that already exists in the fake, and refund_seen_at set: the result must be paid + refunded_after_payout.

findings.claim: held_for_payout has only one wording. The spec requires 'Do wypłaty' when the account is ready, so a ready mentor sees 'Wypłaty gotowe' next to 'Wstrzymane — czeka na dane do wypłaty'.
findings.evidence: SESSION_WORD.held_for_payout is fixed to 'Wstrzymane — czeka na dane do wypłaty' (line 85) and is used at line 226 regardless of setupStatus. The spec Architecture/summary.mjs says `held_for_payout` → 'Wstrzymane — czeka na dane do wypłaty' while the account is not ready, 'Do wypłaty' when ready. The Ready/Many stories render held_for_payout rows with setupStatus 'ready', which shows the contradiction. There is no story for the 'failed' or 'cancelled' rows, although the spec requires 'a story for each'.
findings.fix: Choose the held_for_payout wording from setupStatus ('Do wypłaty', neutral tone, when ready). Add stories for held_for_payout in the ready state, failed and cancelled (MIXED fixture).

findings.claim: The retry-limit test does not prove the backoff schedule. It overwrites next_attempt_at before every run because transferOwed selects candidates with the DB clock, not deps.now.
findings.evidence: Lines 304-308 run `update payouts set next_attempt_at=now()` before each transferOwed and never assert next_attempt_at ≈ attempt time + 1/5/15/60 min. writeFailure could compute any delay and the test would still pass. The root cause is the candidate query in transfers.mjs lines 384-393, which uses `now()` while claimPayout uses deps.now (line 164), so a fake clock cannot drive the job. Lines 186 and 222 use the same workaround. The spec edge case requires 'retried after backoff (fake clock)'.
findings.fix: Pass the deps clock into the candidate query ($n instead of now()), as retryRefunds does with clock(deps). Then rewrite the test to advance only the fake clock. Assert next_attempt_at - updated_at equals 1, 5, 15 and 60 minutes, and assert that a run before the due time makes no transfers.create call.

findings.claim: The recorded manual 390 px / two-mentor check predates the last changes to the UI it verifies, and the mentor-B check only covers a mentor with no paid request.
findings.evidence: manual-check-result.json and the screenshots are dated 10:18-10:19. fix5 (timestamps.txt 16:15-16:21) then changed app/mentor/page.tsx, app/mentor/payouts/page.tsx, lib/payouts/server.ts, lib/payouts/summary.mjs and MentorPayouts.tsx (mtimes 16:16-16:19). The recorded 'porzucony onboarding' text ('Stripe sprawdza dane … Nic nie trzeba robić') is the old copy, which the detailsSubmitted variant now replaces. Step 'B: … (przekierowanie na /mentor)' shows that B had no paid request, so the spec check 'B opens /mentor/payouts?stripe=return … sees only B's state' with B owning an account was not exercised.
findings.fix: Re-run lekcja-21/qa/manual-check.e2e.mjs against the current code. Give mentor B a paid request and their own pending account, open A's return URL and A's fake onboarding link as B, and record the new result and screenshots.

findings.claim: The money-math and state-rule tests are minified onto one line per test (also payouts-money, payouts-schema and payouts-onboarding), against the repo's test formatting, which makes the risk-high evidence hard to review.
findings.evidence: amounts.test.mjs packs 5 tests into lines 5-9 with no spaces or line breaks, e.g. `test("share uses integer floor commission",()=>{for(const [a,b,want] of [...])assert.equal(...)})`. payouts-money.test.mjs lines 44, 82 and 109, payouts-onboarding.test.mjs lines 9-24 and payouts-schema.test.mjs lines 6-10 are the same. By contrast, payouts-webhook.test.mjs, payouts-jobs.test.mjs and the existing tests/db/payments-*.test.mjs use normal formatting. Round 1 F6 asked for the same fix in production code.
findings.fix: Reformat these files like payouts-jobs.test.mjs: one statement per line and a table-driven test with named cases for the share math (1→1, x/0 bps, 10000 bps→0, 15000/1000→13500, 199/333→193, 500000/9999→50).

findings.claim: In the pending state with details submitted, the page says 'Nic nie trzeba robić' and hides the Stripe button. That is wrong when Stripe has requirements due after submission, which brief rule 1 counts as pending.
findings.evidence: Lines 158-161: pending && detailsSubmitted → SETUP.pending ('Nic nie trzeba robić…') and actionLabel=null, so only 'Odśwież stan' is shown. details_submitted stays true when Stripe later asks for more information (payouts_enabled false), and nothing in mentor_payout_accounts records requirements. Meanwhile /mentor shows PayoutSetupPrompt for the same account (askForPayouts is true while not ready), so the two pages give the mentor contradictory instructions.
findings.fix: Either keep the secondary 'Dokończ konfigurację w Stripe' button in pending+detailsSubmitted, or store requirements.currently_due/past_due (or disabled_reason) in applyAccountObject and show the action variant when it is non-empty. Use the same wording on /mentor.

findings.claim: The payout prompt and status line render before the page's h1 and outside the editor column, which breaks the DOM order the file header documents. The header also still says 'Bez wzmianki o wypłatach (Z36)'.
findings.evidence:
MentorPageForm renders the h1 'Twoja strona' itself (packages/ui/src/product/e01/Mentor.tsx line 408) and puts banners after it through the `notice` slot. page.tsx lines 66-74 render PayoutSetupPrompt /

before . The header (lines 8, 11-12) says 'nagłówek → baner → panel linku → formularz' and 'Bez wzmianki o wypłatach (Z36)'. The `oczekują na dane do wypłaty` branch on line 71 is dead code, because askForPayouts is false only when the account is ready.
findings.fix: Pass the prompt (and the 'Wypłaty: gotowe' link) through the `notice` prop together with NoAvailabilityNotice. Drop the dead branch and update the header comment.

findings.claim: The design-system package now imports next/navigation, although packages/ui is plain React and does not depend on next.
findings.evidence: MentorPayouts.tsx line 6 imports useRouter from 'next/navigation' and uses it in RouterRefreshButton (line 256). It is the only next import in packages/ui/src (grep), packages/ui/package.json has no next dependency, and packages/ui/AGENTS.md line 3 says 'Plain React … the Next.js block … does not apply here'. Every story passes onRefresh, so the router path that /mentor/payouts actually uses is never rendered in Storybook.
findings.fix: Keep MentorPayouts framework-free: require onRefresh, and provide it from a small 'use client' wrapper in app/mentor/payouts that calls router.refresh(). Alternatively, render the refresh as a link to the same URL.

findings.claim: The E2E 'paid total' check does not prove that 'Wypłacone do tej pory' shows 135 zł, because the session row shows 135 zł in every state.
findings.evidence: Line 136 waits for the label 'Wypłacone do tej pory', which is always rendered (MentorPayouts.tsx line 199). Line 137 matches /135\s?zł/ anywhere in <main>, and the request row's Amount is 135 zł whether or not anything was paid. The E2E also never checks that /mentor/payouts redirects to /mentor before the first payment, or that /mentor/requests still works while the prompt is visible (both in the spec's E2E list).
findings.fix: Read the value of the 'Wypłacone do tej pory' description item, for example with locator('dd') after that dt, and assert 135 zł and 'Do wypłaty' 0 zł. Add the redirect check before payment and a /mentor/requests visit while the prompt is shown.

findings.claim: Several spec edge-case rows are still not proven by any test.
findings.evidence: Same-second account.updated is tested only in the order ready→pending (lines 59-67); the spec asks for both delivery orders. No test applies account.updated ready and then runs transferOwed ('Account ready via webhook → next run transfers'). No test checks that a request insert is not blocked during concurrent onboarding clicks. The fake transfers.list (tests/payments/fake-stripe.mjs) ignores created.gte and always returns has_more:false, so the pagination in findExistingTransfer is never exercised. The 'stalled worker' lease test (payouts-transfer.test.mjs lines 236-252) has no earlier create in flight, so it does not show that two workers share one key.
findings.fix: Add the missing order, a webhook→transferOwed test and an onboarding test with a concurrent paidRequest insert. Make the fake paginate (limit and has_more) and add a take-over test with more than 100 transfers. In the lease test, create the transfer with key v1 before re-claiming, then assert one transfer and the same idempotencyKey.

findings.claim: The retrieval guard compares the DB clock with the app clock (resync_requested_at = now() against asOf = deps.now()).
findings.evidence: Lines 30 and 40 set resync_requested_at with the DB `now()`, while line 33 compares it with $6 = asOf from deps.now()/new Date() (sync line 59, job line 441). If the app host runs behind the DB, every retrieval after a webhook is discarded and the flag never clears. The webhook test at payouts-webhook.test.mjs line 71 needs a +1 s DB offset to work around this.
findings.fix: Take t0 from the database (`select now()` or clock_timestamp()) before accounts.retrieve and compare with it, or set resync_requested_at from the same app clock that is passed in.

findings.claim: The new webhook code does not follow the module's style: SQL is minified, onRefundSeen, onTransferCreated and onTransferReversed have no JSDoc, and there is no blank line between them. accounts.mjs has a Cyrillic JSDoc fragment and a misleading comment.
findings.evidence: webhook.mjs line 147: `"update payments set refund_seen_at=coalesce(refund_seen_at,$2),updated_at=$2 where id=$1"`, while line ~196 has the same SQL formatted. Lines 236/255 have no `/** @param … */`, unlike onDispute. accounts.mjs line 75: '@param {any} deps база, клиент Stripe'. Line 38 says 'A retrieval racing a webhook is discarded', but that branch handles a webhook that was not applied. transfers.mjs resyncAccounts/resolveExpiredFinalLeases have no JSDoc. In the stories, PendingAbandoned and ActionRequired have identical args, and the header still says 'Agent test (lekcja 06) … no backend'.
findings.fix: Format the SQL and add JSDoc as in the neighbouring handlers. Fix the Cyrillic and the comment, remove the duplicate story and the draft header.
